Select rows with the smallest values of a variable

Source: R/slice.R
slice_min.tbl_gpu.Rd

Keeps the n (or prop fraction of) rows with the smallest order_by values, similar to dplyr::slice_min(). Ungrouped, group_by()-grouped, and by= calls with a plain order_by (a bare column, or an expression the mutate/filter IR recognizes) all run entirely on the GPU (Phase 5, task W7): ungrouped via a top-k cut plus a sort of the survivors when the key is numeric or a date and n is a small share of the rows, otherwise a stable sort (with cudf::rank() for ties); grouped/by= on such a key by stable radix sorts of the row positions and per-group ranks, other grouped/by= keys via a per-group window desugar (see R/slice.R's module docs for the exact group-ordering rules, including by='s first-appearance-order rule, which applies here too, not just to the positional slice_*()s). An unsupported order_by expression (one the IR can't parse) still transparently falls back to CPU evaluation (see gpu_fallback()).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
slice_min(
  .data,
  order_by,
  ...,
  n,
  prop,
  by = NULL,
  with_ties = TRUE,
  na_rm = FALSE
)

Arguments

.data

A tbl_gpu object created by tbl_gpu().

order_by

Column (or IR-supported expression) to rank by.

...

Not used; for extensibility, must be empty.

n, prop

As for slice_head.tbl_gpu().

by

Optional on-the-fly grouping columns, GPU-native (Phase 5, task W7) – see slice_head.tbl_gpu()'s by docs.

with_ties

If TRUE (the default), ties at the cutoff are all kept (the result can have more than n rows); if FALSE, ties are broken by original row position and the result has exactly n rows (or fewer if .data is smaller).

na_rm

If FALSE (the default), NA values in order_by sort last (for both slice_min() and slice_max()) and can appear in the result once n/prop reaches past the non-NA count. If TRUE, NA rows are always excluded.

Value

A tbl_gpu object with the selected rows, in ascending order_by order (grouped: ascending order_by order within each group's own block).
